title: Junior Estimator/Contract Administrator
content_text:
About us
Burland Contractors is an established Victorian civil and commercial landscape contractor. Our projects are varied, we work across education, health, commercial, retail and residential projects, delivering everything from quiet spaces of reflection, bustling playgrounds and functional hardscapes. We're a growing business that is big enough to be trusted yet small enough to be agile.
About the role
This is a varied, office-based role combining estimating and contract/project administration. You'll work with our Senior Estimator and project team on reviewing construction drawings, specifications and tender documents, completing quantity take-offs from landscape and construction drawings, and assisting with the preparation of project estimates and quotations.
Key responsibilities
- Reviewing construction drawings, specifications and tender documents
- Completing quantity take-offs from landscape and construction drawings
- Assisting with the preparation of project estimates and quotations
- Sending requests for pricing to suppliers and subcontractors
- Comparing and recording supplier quotations
- Maintaining current supplier, material and subcontractor pricing
- Assisting in the development and maintenance of our estimating price book
- Preparing tender documentation, inclusions, exclusions and supporting information
- Setting up and maintaining project and tender records
- Maintaining contracts, variations and other commercial project documentation
About you
- Strong attention to detail and good numerical skills
- Confidence using Excel and computer systems
- Good written and verbal communication
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
- An understanding of construction and how projects are priced and delivered
- The ability to read construction drawings, or the willingness to learn
- Experience in landscaping, civil or commercial construction would be highly regarded
- Experience with estimating or construction management software would be highly regarded, but is not essential
Apply through SEEK with your resume and a short introduction telling us about your experience and why the role interests you.

title: Technical and Asset Officer
content_text:
Make an impact on the infrastructure that supports our community
Lower Eyre Council is looking for a Technical & Asset Officer to join our Works team in Cummins.
This is a varied, hands-on role for someone who enjoys combining technical work with practical problem-solving. You’ll work across civil infrastructure, minor projects, asset management and GIS, with the opportunity to get out in the field as well as work alongside our Works and Major Projects teams.
Whether your background is in civil engineering, construction, surveying, asset management or you’ve built strong practical experience in the field, we’d love to hear from you. While relevant industry experience is highly valued, we also welcome recent engineering graduates eager to put their knowledge into practice and build their careers with our team.
About the role
Working closely with the Works Manager, Major Projects team, Works Coordinators and field staff, you’ll provide technical and project support across the delivery, maintenance and renewal of Council infrastructure.
No two days will necessarily look the same. You might be undertaking a site inspection, preparing a design or cost estimate, reviewing access or drainage requirements, coordinating a minor infrastructure project, or updating Council’s asset and GIS information.
Some of the things you’ll be involved in:
- Providing practical technical advice and support to Council staff and contractors
- Undertaking site inspections, basic surveying and footpath design
- Preparing plans, quantities and cost estimates for minor works
- Coordinating footpath construction, minor asset renewals, road resealing and line marking programs
- Collecting and analysing traffic data across Council’s road network
- Assessing applications for works within Council road reserves
- Assisting with heavy vehicle access requests and road manager responses
- Providing technical input into development and land division referrals, including access, drainage and impacts on Council infrastructure
- Managing Before You Dig enquiries and liaising with utility providers
- Collecting and maintaining accurate asset and GIS information
- Supporting the maintenance and renewal of Council’s internal communications radio system
- The scope of responsibilities and level of guidance will reflect the successful applicant’s skills and experience.
We’re looking for someone who is practical, organised and comfortable working with both field and office-based teams.
You’ll ideally bring:
- A qualification in civil engineering, construction, surveying or asset management, or relevant practical experience
-    Experience in civil infrastructure, construction, maintenance, technical support or minor project coordination
- A working knowledge of roads, footpaths and drainage
- The ability to interpret plans and undertake basic surveying, design and quantity calculations
- Confidence working with technical information, spreadsheets and asset data
- Good communication, organisation and problem-solving skills
- Initiative, sound judgement and strong attention to detail
- The ability to manage competing priorities and work collaboratively with others
- A current Class C driver’s licence
- A Construction Industry White Card, or willingness to obtain one
Graduate applicants are encouraged to highlight relevant university projects, work placements and technical skills, along with their interest in developing practical infrastructure experience.
Why join Lower Eyre Council?
Working with Council gives you the opportunity to be involved in projects and services that you can see making a difference in the communities around you.
Based in Cummins, you’ll have the opportunity to build your career while enjoying everything the region has to offer.
You’ll work alongside experienced engineering and local government professionals across a broad range of projects and infrastructure, with opportunities to strengthen your practical skills and pursue future career progression within Council.
Applications close: 5.00pm, Monday 02 November 2026.
Enquiries
For a confidential discussion regarding this position, please contact the Director Infrastructure & Development, Brad-Lee Tolley on 8676 0400, or visit https://www.lowereyrepeninsula.sa.gov.au/
